---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: TOCTOU race condition in get() key check
DESCRIPTION: The `if key not in self._store:` check occurs outside the lock. Another thread can delete or modify the entry between the check and the lock acquisition, leading to a KeyError or inconsistent state when the lock is finally acquired.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Move the key existence check inside the `with self._lock:` block, or remove it and handle KeyError/expiration directly within the lock.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Inconsistent lock acquisition in invalidate_older_than()
DESCRIPTION: The method acquires and releases the lock inside the loop for each deletion. This causes unnecessary contention and leaves the cache in a partially updated state between iterations if another thread modifies it concurrently.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Acquire the lock once at the start of the method, perform all deletions, and release it before returning.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Unbounded growth when max_size is zero or negative
DESCRIPTION: The condition `if len(self._store) > self._max_size:` never triggers if `max_size <= 0`, causing the cache to grow without bound and eventually exhaust memory.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add a validation check in `__init__` to raise `ValueError` if `max_size <= 0`, or handle it by immediately evicting or rejecting inserts.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Expired entries inflate cache size beyond max_size
DESCRIPTION: `put()` checks `len(self._store)` against `max_size`, but expired entries are only removed lazily in `get()`. The cache can grow indefinitely past `max_size` if new keys are inserted while old ones sit expired.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Implement periodic background eviction or check expiration count during `put()`, or document that `max_size` applies to total entries, not just live ones.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Non-reentrant lock risks deadlock on nested calls
DESCRIPTION: `threading.Lock()` is not reentrant. If any method calls another method that also acquires the lock (e.g., `get()` calling `put()` or vice versa), it will deadlock.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `threading.RLock()` instead of `threading.Lock()` to allow safe nested locking within the same thread.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Clock drift vulnerability using time.time() for TTL
DESCRIPTION: `time.time()` can jump backwards due to NTP adjustments or system clock changes, causing TTL calculations to behave unpredictably or entries to expire prematurely or never.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace `time.time()` with `time.monotonic()` for all timestamp comparisons to ensure strictly increasing time values.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: performance
TITLE: Redundant move_to_end() call in put()
DESCRIPTION: Assigning a value to an existing key in `OrderedDict` automatically moves it to the end in modern Python versions. The explicit call is unnecessary and adds minor overhead.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Remove `self._store.move_to_end(key)` from `put()` as it is redundant.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Negative or zero TTL causes immediate expiration
DESCRIPTION: If `ttl_seconds` is passed as 0 or negative, `time.time() - ts > self._ttl` will immediately evaluate to True, causing all entries to be deleted upon retrieval.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Validate `ttl_seconds > 0` in `__init__` and raise `ValueError` for invalid inputs.

---END---

Oto zsynthezyzowana lista deduplikowanych ustaleń:

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Race Condition in `get()` — Check Outside Lock
DESCRIPTION: The `get()` method checks `if key not in self._store:` before acquiring the lock. Another thread can delete, insert, or replace the entry between this unprotected check and the subsequent locked access, causing a `KeyError` on the `self._store[key]` line or returning stale/inconsistent data. When the staleness check happens inside the lock but the membership test is outside, concurrent `put()` calls can interleave, causing `get()` to read stale or incorrect data if an entry is deleted and re-inserted by another thread. This defeats the purpose of locking entirely for the read path.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Move the `if key not in self._store` check inside the `with self._lock:` block so membership test and read are atomic. Perform all reads and writes under a single lock acquisition in `get()`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Non-Atomic Locking in `invalidate_older_than()` — Lock Per-Iteration
DESCRIPTION: The method iterates over `list(self._store.keys())` and reads entries outside the lock, only acquiring it per-key for deletion. This breaks atomicity multiple ways: (1) Between snapshotting keys and accessing entries, concurrent threads may delete/replace keys, causing `KeyError`; (2) Per-key lock acquire/release allows concurrent `put()`/`get()` operations to interleave mid-scan, leaving the dict inconsistent; (3) Returned removal count becomes unreliable — items may be double-counted, skipped, or create races where concurrent calls try to delete the same key (second raises `KeyError`); (4) Excessive lock contention. Concurrent calls to `invalidate_older_than()` or concurrent `get()` operations (which also delete expired entries) can fail with `KeyError`.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Acquire the lock once at the top of the method before iteration, perform all deletions inside a single lock acquisition, then release. Alternatively, use `self._store.pop(key, None)` instead of `del self._store[key]`, or hold the lock for the entire operation to ensure atomic state inspection and modification.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Clock Drift Causes Unreliable TTL Expiration
DESCRIPTION: The code uses `time.time()` for TTL calculations, which can jump backwards due to NTP adjustments or manual system clock changes. When the system clock jumps backward, existing cached entries may be considered expired immediately. When the clock jumps forward, expired entries may never expire, breaking cache consistency guarantees and potentially serving stale data indefinitely.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace all `time.time()` calls with `time.monotonic()` for reliable, monotonic time tracking independent of system clock adjustments.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Missing Input Validation for Cache Parameters
DESCRIPTION: `__init__` accepts negative or zero values for `max_size` and `ttl_seconds` without validation. When `max_size <= 0`, the cache either refuses to store any entries or exhibits undefined behavior. When `ttl_seconds <= 0`, every `get()` call finds all entries expired, making the cache non-functional. These invalid parameters are silently accepted, leading to silent cache failure in production.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add validation in `__init__` to raise `ValueError` if `max_size <= 0` or `ttl_seconds <= 0`, rejecting all non-positive inputs.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: No Eviction of Expired Entries During `put()`
DESCRIPTION: When the cache is full and a new entry must be added, `put()` evicts the least-recently-used entry, which may still be valid. However, many expired entries could remain in the cache consuming space. The effective cache capacity is reduced by these expired entries, which are only cleaned up lazily on `get()` or explicit `invalidate_older_than()` calls. This violates expected TTL cache semantics where expired entries should not consume space.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Before checking size and evicting LRU entries, optionally purge expired entries first. Alternatively, evict expired entries preferentially over valid LRU entries when capacity is reached.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: TTL Not Reset on Cache Access
DESCRIPTION: The `get()` method updates the LRU order via `move_to_end` when retrieving an entry, but does not update the stored timestamp. Entries expire based on creation time regardless of access frequency, which contradicts standard TTL-on-access cache behavior where frequently-accessed entries should have their TTL renewed.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Update the timestamp tuple in `_store` when `get()` successfully retrieves a non-expired entry, or document that TTL is strictly creation-time based, not access-time based.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: memory
TITLE: Memory Spike and Performance Issues from Key Snapshot Creation
DESCRIPTION: `invalidate_older_than()` calls `list(self._store.keys())`, creating a full in-memory copy of all cache keys. For large caches, this doubles memory usage temporarily and can trigger garbage collection pauses or OOM conditions. Additionally, the method always performs a full scan instead of stopping early; while OrderedDict is ordered by insertion/access, `move_to_end` on `get()` disrupts timestamp ordering so early termination is unreliable. The O(n) cost is not documented and can be wasteful for large caches.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Iterate directly over `self._store.items()` or use a generator to avoid materializing the entire key list in memory. Document the O(n) cost, or break early if strict LRU ordering is acceptable as a proxy for age.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: LRU Order Inconsistency After Bulk Removal
DESCRIPTION: `invalidate_older_than()` removes old entries but leaves remaining items in original insertion order, breaking strict LRU semantics. This can cause unexpected eviction patterns when the cache reaches capacity.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Rebuild the LRU order by moving remaining items to the end, or document that bulk removals do not preserve LRU ordering.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Ambiguous TTL Semantics in Method Documentation
DESCRIPTION: The method name `invalidate_older_than` and implementation compare against creation time (`ts`), but TTL caches often imply expiration based on last access. This ambiguity can mislead consumers expecting access-time-based expiration rather than insertion-time-based.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Rename to `invalidate_older_than_creation` for clarity, or explicitly document that age is measured from insertion time, not last access.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Unhandled Negative Age Parameter in `invalidate_older_than()`
DESCRIPTION: `invalidate_older_than()` accepts negative `age_seconds` without validation. Negative values result in a cutoff time in the future, causing zero removals and silently masking caller errors.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Validate `age_seconds` at method start and raise `ValueError` for negative inputs, or clamp to zero.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: No Metrics or Logging for Cache Behavior
DESCRIPTION: The cache provides no visibility into hit/miss rates, eviction counts, or expired-entry removal counts. Operators cannot tune `max_size` or `ttl_seconds` or debug cache issues without external instrumentation.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add counters for cache hits, misses, LRU evictions, TTL evictions, and expose them via a `stats()` method or configurable logging.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: data
TITLE: Loss of Type Information in Return Type
DESCRIPTION: `get()` returns `object | None`, providing no type safety. Callers must cast or assert on every retrieval, increasing runtime type error risk and reducing IDE autocomplete quality.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Make `TTLCache` generic using `typing.Generic[T]` so callers get properly typed return values from `get()`.

---END---

# Deduplicated Code Review Findings

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: TOCTOU race condition in `get` method
DESCRIPTION: The key existence check (`if key not in self._store`) occurs outside the lock. If another thread deletes the key between the check and lock acquisition, `self._store[key]` will raise a KeyError, breaking under concurrent read/write workloads.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Move the key existence check and subsequent access inside the `with self._lock:` block to ensure atomic access.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: `invalidate_older_than` acquires lock per-key and reads outside lock, causing TOCTOU and contention
DESCRIPTION: The method iterates over a snapshot of keys outside any lock, then acquires the lock only for deletion inside the loop. This creates two race conditions: (1) between snapshot and deletion, another thread may have already deleted the key, causing KeyError on `del self._store[key]`; (2) timestamp reads (`ts, _ = self._store[key]`) occur without holding the lock, exposing the method to concurrent modifications. Additionally, acquiring and releasing the lock inside the loop creates severe lock contention under high concurrency, drastically reducing throughput during bulk operations.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Acquire `self._lock` once at the method start, then iterate, read values, and delete while holding the lock throughout. This eliminates TOCTOU races and reduces lock contention.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: `put` evicts entries spuriously during concurrent overwrites
DESCRIPTION: When `put` is called with an existing key at max capacity, the assignment overwrites the value without growing the store size. However, with concurrent puts racing in, the combined effect can cause spurious eviction of other valid entries due to unconditional `move_to_end` followed by the size check, leaving the cache in an inconsistent state.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check `if key not in self._store` before the overflow guard to clearly separate new-key insertion (which may trigger eviction) from in-place updates (which should not).

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: data
TITLE: System clock adjustments break TTL accuracy and entry lifetime guarantees
DESCRIPTION: Using `time.time()` for elapsed time calculations is vulnerable to NTP synchronization, manual clock changes, DST transitions, and leap seconds. Clock jumps can cause entries to expire prematurely, never expire, or appear newer than they are, corrupting cache consistency across distributed or long-running processes.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace all `time.time()` calls with `time.monotonic()` to guarantee monotonically increasing time measurements.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: `get` does not update LRU order when deleting expired entries
DESCRIPTION: When `put` inserts a new entry exceeding `max_size`, `popitem(last=False)` correctly evicts the LRU item. However, `get` silently deletes expired entries without updating LRU ordering, potentially leaving stale entries that still count against `max_size`, degrading cache effectiveness.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Delete expired entries immediately upon detection and update LRU ordering, or document that expired entries consume capacity until explicitly accessed or invalidated.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Zero or negative `max_size` causes perpetual cache emptiness
DESCRIPTION: If `max_size <= 0`, every `put` call will immediately evict the entry it just inserted (since `len > 0` is immediately true), leaving the cache permanently empty. There is no validation in `__init__`.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add `if max_size < 1: raise ValueError("max_size must be >= 1")` in `__init__`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Negative or zero `ttl_seconds` makes all entries immediately expired
DESCRIPTION: A `ttl_seconds` of `0` or negative means `time.time() - ts > self._ttl` is always true immediately after insertion, so every `get` will return `None` and delete the entry, wasting CPU cycles on constant cache thrashing. There is no guard in `__init__`.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add `if ttl_seconds <= 0: raise ValueError("ttl_seconds must be positive")` in `__init__`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: `invalidate_older_than` with `age_seconds <= 0` wipes entire cache
DESCRIPTION: If `age_seconds <= 0`, the cutoff equals or exceeds `time.time()`, so every entry's timestamp will be less than the cutoff and the entire cache will be cleared. This surprising behavior is undocumented with no safeguard.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Document this behavior explicitly, or add a guard: `if age_seconds <= 0: raise ValueError("age_seconds must be positive")`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Expired entries accumulate and bypass `max_size` capacity limit
DESCRIPTION: TTL validation only occurs lazily on `get`. If a key is never accessed again after expiry, the stale entry remains in `_store` indefinitely and counts against `max_size`, potentially evicting live entries and defeating the intended capacity guarantee.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Implement periodic background eviction with a sweeper thread, validate TTL during `put` to filter stale entries, or document this limitation as a behavioral caveat.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: No cache hit/miss/eviction metrics or logging
DESCRIPTION: For a cache serving API responses, there is no instrumentation for hit rate, miss rate, TTL evictions, LRU evictions, or current size. Without this, diagnosing cache effectiveness, capacity planning, and production performance regressions is impossible.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add counters (e.g., `self._hits`, `self._misses`, `self._lru_evictions`, `self._ttl_evictions`) updated atomically under the lock, and expose them via a `stats()` method or standard metrics interface.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Absolute TTL does not refresh on cache hits
DESCRIPTION: The `get` method updates the LRU order on successful hits but does not reset the entry's timestamp. This results in absolute expiration rather than sliding TTL, which may not match expected API caching behavior where hits extend the lifetime.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Update the timestamp tuple on successful hits if sliding TTL is desired, or document the absolute TTL behavior clearly.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: `get` returns `None` ambiguously for missing vs. expired entries
DESCRIPTION: Both a cache miss and a TTL expiry return `None`, making it impossible for the caller to distinguish between "key was never set" and "key existed but expired." This can lead to incorrect retry or fallback logic in callers.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Return a sentinel object, raise a distinct exception, or document the ambiguity explicitly and require callers to handle it.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Unbounded object storage enables memory exhaustion
DESCRIPTION: The cache stores arbitrary Python objects without size limits or type restrictions. Malicious or large payloads can be injected via `put`, enabling uncontrolled memory growth and potential denial of service attacks.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Implement a maximum entry size limit, validate object types or sizes before insertion, or use a serialization layer to enforce memory bounds.

SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Open redirect via unvalidated redirect_url parameter

An attacker can craft a login link with a malicious `redirect_url` pointing to a phishing site, and after successful authentication, the user will be seamlessly redirected to the attacker's domain, where their session token can be stolen or they can be socially engineered.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Validate the `redirect_url` against a strict whitelist of allowed domains or paths before including it in the redirect. Reject any URL pointing to an external origin.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Timing attack vulnerability in password hash comparison
DESCRIPTION: The `login` function compares the computed hash against the stored hash using the `==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. An attacker can statistically measure response times across many requests to deduce the correct hash one character at a time, especially in network-accessible scenarios.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `hmac.compare_digest()` or `secrets.compare_digest()` for constant-time string comparison to prevent timing side-channel attacks.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Session token exposed in URL query parameters
DESCRIPTION: The session token is embedded in the redirect URL as a query parameter (`?session=...`). Query strings are recorded in browser history, server access logs, proxy logs, and transmitted in `Referer` headers when users navigate away. Any of these leakage paths allows attackers to hijack sessions.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Transmit the session token via a secure, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` cookie or through a short-lived authorization code that is exchanged server-side, rather than exposing it in the query string.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Sessions never expire
DESCRIPTION: Once created, a session token persists in the `SESSIONS` dictionary indefinitely with no TTL, expiration timestamp, or cleanup mechanism. Stolen or leaked tokens remain valid forever, maximizing the window for session hijacking and violating security best practices.

SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Global SESSIONS dictionary is not thread-safe and not suitable for multi-process deployments
DESCRIPTION: The `SESSIONS` dictionary is a global mutable object accessed without synchronization primitives. In multi-threaded servers, concurrent requests can cause race conditions and data corruption. SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: memory
TITLE: In-memory session storage causes unbounded memory leak
DESCRIPTION: Because sessions are added to the `SESSIONS` dictionary but never removed, the dictionary grows monotonically with every call to `create_session`. In a long-running process, this constitutes an unbounded memory leak that will eventually exhaust available RAM and crash the service.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Implement session expiration and deletion logic (e.g., via `verify_session` consuming the token or a background cleanup task). In production, use Redis or a similar store with built-in TTL and automatic eviction.

SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Insecure salt concatenation in password hashing
DESCRIPTION: The `hash_password` function concatenates password and salt directly (`password + salt`) before hashing. While better than no salt, this is not a standard or robust method. SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: No session invalidation or logout mechanism
DESCRIPTION: There is no function to revoke or delete a session token. Users cannot log out, and compromised tokens cannot be administratively invalidated or revoked, violating the principle of least privilege for session lifecycle management.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add a `revoke_session(token)` function that removes the token from `SESSIONS` and call it on logout or when a security event is detected.

SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case

DESCRIPTION: The `login` and `create_session` functions do not validate that `user_id` or `password` are non-empty strings. Empty strings could create valid sessions mapped to empty user IDs, or an empty password could hash and match if an account has no password set.

# Deduplicated Code Review Findings

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Unsynchronized concurrent access to `_results` list causes data races
DESCRIPTION: Multiple worker threads call `self._results.append(...)` without synchronization. While CPython's GIL makes a single append atomic, `get_results()` returns a live reference to the internal list. Callers iterating over it while workers append concurrently can observe partially-updated lists, raise `RuntimeError: list changed size during iteration`, or corrupt data. Callers can also directly modify the returned list, causing further race conditions.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Protect all accesses to `_results` with a `threading.Lock`. Have `get_results()` return a shallow copy `return list(self._results)` taken under that lock.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Non-thread-safe `_stop` flag causes visibility and race condition issues
DESCRIPTION: The `_stop` boolean is read and written across threads without synchronization. While CPython's GIL makes assignment atomic, there is no memory-visibility guarantee that workers will see the updated value promptly, especially on other Python implementations. This delays or prevents shutdown signal delivery.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace `_stop` with a `threading.Event` (`_stop_event`); workers check `_stop_event.is_set()` and `shutdown()` calls `_stop_event.set()`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: memory
TITLE: Unbounded `_results` list causes indefinite memory growth
DESCRIPTION: The `_results` list appends every job result with no cleanup or size limit. In long-running pools, memory consumption grows unboundedly until the process crashes or starves the system.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Provide a `clear_results()` method, use a bounded `collections.deque(maxlen=N)`, or document a consume-and-clear contract for callers.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: memory
TITLE: Unbounded job queue defaults to infinite size
DESCRIPTION: `queue.Queue()` defaults to unbounded size. If jobs are submitted faster than workers process them, memory usage grows indefinitely until the process crashes.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Initialize the queue with a reasonable `maxsize` parameter to apply backpressure and prevent runaway growth.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: `shutdown()` leaves queued jobs silently unprocessed
DESCRIPTION: Setting `_stop = True` causes workers to exit at the next timeout boundary (up to 1 second later). Any jobs still queued are never executed and no error is raised. Callers have no visibility into abandoned work.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Before setting the stop flag, drain remaining queue items via `_queue.join()` (requires `task_done()` calls), or add a `wait=True` parameter that synchronizes completion.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Workers never call `queue.task_done()`, breaking join semantics
DESCRIPTION: `queue.Queue.join()` blocks until every put item has a corresponding `task_done()` call. Since `_worker_loop` never calls `task_done()`, any use of `_queue.join()` to wait for completion will deadlock indefinitely. This prevents clean drain-before-stop patterns.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add `self._queue.task_done()` in a `finally` block inside `_worker_loop`, after the job is processed (success or failure).

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Multiple `shutdown()` calls cause `RuntimeError` on re-join
DESCRIPTION: Calling `shutdown()` twice attempts to join already-joined threads, raising a `RuntimeError`. This breaks idempotent cleanup and crashes graceful shutdown sequences.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add a `_shutdown_flag` and use `threading.Lock` to guard `shutdown()`, making it idempotent and thread-safe.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: `shutdown()` deadlocks indefinitely with long-running or blocked jobs
DESCRIPTION: `w.join()` blocks indefinitely with no timeout. If a submitted job never returns (infinite loop, blocking I/O, internal deadlock), `shutdown()` hangs forever. No mechanism exists to interrupt or kill worker threads.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Pass a `timeout` parameter to `w.join()` and document that submitted callables must be finite, or expose a cancel/interrupt mechanism.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: `submit()` allows enqueuing jobs after `shutdown()` is called
DESCRIPTION: Jobs can be enqueued after `shutdown()` has been called. Since workers have already exited, these jobs are lost silently or processed by lingering threads. No exception is raised and the caller may believe work was accepted.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check the shutdown flag in `submit()` and raise `RuntimeError("pool is shut down")` if the pool is no longer active.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: `fn.__name__` raises `AttributeError` for lambdas and `functools.partial`
DESCRIPTION: Lambda objects have `__name__ == '<lambda>'` (acceptable but ambiguous), while `functools.partial` objects lack `__name__` entirely, causing an `AttributeError` that crashes the worker thread. This halts processing for that job and makes debugging difficult.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `getattr(fn, '__name__', repr(fn))` to safely retrieve the function name without raising exceptions.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Zero or negative `num_workers` creates a broken pool silently
DESCRIPTION: Passing `num_workers <= 0` results in an empty worker list. Submitted jobs are queued forever and never executed. `shutdown()` returns immediately. No `ValueError` is raised and the caller may assume work is being done.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add validation in `__init__`: `if num_workers < 1: raise ValueError(f"num_workers must be >= 1, got {num_workers}")`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Error results are indistinguishable from legitimate string return values
DESCRIPTION: When a job raises an exception, the result is stored as a plain string `"ERROR: <msg>"`. If a job legitimately returns a string beginning with `"ERROR: "`, the caller cannot tell success from failure, making the API unreliable.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Store results as typed objects, e.g., a `JobResult(status, value)` dataclass with explicit `"ok"` / `"error"` status, or use a custom `JobError` sentinel class.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: Exceptions in jobs are silently swallowed with no logging
DESCRIPTION: Worker exceptions are caught and stored as strings but never logged. If no one calls `get_results()` and inspects every entry, failures are invisible. In long-running pools this makes debugging extremely difficult.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add `logging.exception(...)` or `logging.error(...)` inside the except block so failures surface in application logs immediately.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: performance
TITLE: Polling loop with timeout wastes CPU and delays shutdown
DESCRIPTION: Workers rely on `queue.get(timeout=1.0)` and spin on `queue.Empty`. This delays shutdown by up to 1 second per worker and wastes CPU cycles during idle periods.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `threading.Event` to signal workers to wake up immediately, or use `queue.join()` with sentinel values for clean termination.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Daemon flag contradicts explicit `shutdown()` contract
DESCRIPTION: Threads are marked as `daemon=True`, causing them to terminate abruptly when the main thread exits. This contradicts the explicit `shutdown()` join contract and can cause silent data loss or incomplete processing.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Remove `daemon=True` if `shutdown()` is intended to be called, or document that `shutdown()` is optional and daemons will be killed on exit.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: design
TITLE: No way to retrieve result for a specific submitted job
DESCRIPTION: All results are aggregated in a single list keyed only by function name. Callers cannot correlate a result to a specific `submit()` call. Multiple calls to the same function produce duplicate ambiguous keys, making the API unsuitable for anything beyond fire-and-forget homogeneous jobs.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Return a `Future`-like object from `submit()` that the caller can `.result()` on, or assign a unique job ID and expose `get_result(job_id)`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: design
TITLE: No context manager support (`__enter__` / `__exit__`)
DESCRIPTION: The pool manages threads but is not usable as a context manager, making it easy to forget `shutdown()` calls in exception paths, leading to thread leaks and resource exhaustion.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Implement `__enter__` returning `self` and `__exit__` calling `self.shutdown()` to guarantee cleanup.

Syntetyzuję raporty z trzech recenzentów, łącząc zduplikowane znaleziska i zachowując unikalne:

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: data
TITLE: Missing database commit causes complete data loss
DESCRIPTION: `run_migration` never calls `conn.commit()`. SQLite's default `isolation_level` is `""` (deferred transactions), so `UPDATE` statements execute within an implicit transaction. When `conn.close()` is called in the `finally` block, the uncommitted transaction is rolled back and all changes are silently lost. The function returns a positive `total` count, making the caller believe the migration succeeded when zero rows are actually persisted. Any interruption (crash, manual kill) also results in complete loss of all progress.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Call `conn.commit()` after successfully completing the migration loop and all batches have been updated, or use `conn` as a context manager (`with conn:`) to auto-commit on successful exit.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: No exception handling or transaction rollback on migration failure
DESCRIPTION: If an exception occurs during the migration (e.g., disk full, constraint violation, locked database, schema mismatch), the `finally` block closes the connection without explicitly rolling back the transaction or handling the error. This leaves the database in an undefined state, making it difficult to recover and preventing the caller from understanding what progress was made before failure.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Wrap the migration logic in a `try...except` block and call `conn.rollback()` explicitly in the `except` clause before re-raising the exception. Add logging to indicate which batch completed successfully before the error occurred.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Empty table causes TypeError crash
DESCRIPTION: When the `users` table is empty, `SELECT MAX(id)` returns `None`. The code then attempts `range(0, None, BATCH_SIZE)` which raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`. The migration crashes instead of gracefully handling the empty table case.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check if `max_id` is `None` after `fetchone()` and either return early (no users to backfill) or default to 0 before the range() call.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Off-by-one bug skips the row with id == max_id
DESCRIPTION: The range `range(0, max_id, BATCH_SIZE)` produces windows `[start, start+BATCH_SIZE)`. The last window's upper bound is at most `max_id`, so a user whose `id` exactly equals `max_id` is never selected by the `id >= ? AND id < ?` predicate. This row is silently skipped every time the migration runs.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Change the range to `range(0, max_id + 1, BATCH_SIZE)` so the final batch's upper bound is at least `max_id + 1`, ensuring the row with `id == max_id` is included.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: performance
TITLE: Row-by-row UPDATE statements instead of batch updates
DESCRIPTION: Each user ID in a batch triggers an individual `UPDATE` statement. For a batch of 500 rows, this results in 500 individual round-trips to the database engine, creating significant overhead. A single `UPDATE users SET tier = 'free' WHERE id IN (?, ?, ...)` per batch would reduce round-trips and database/WAL pressure by orders of magnitude.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace the inner loop with a single parameterized `UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (...)` per batch using `conn.execute()` with a constructed placeholder list.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: performance
TITLE: ID range pagination is inefficient for sparse or non-zero-based IDs
DESCRIPTION: The code uses `range(0, max_id, BATCH_SIZE)` to paginate, which assumes user IDs are contiguous integers starting from 0 or 1. If IDs start at a much larger value (e.g., 1,000,000) or have gaps, the query will repeatedly scan empty ranges, wasting I/O and CPU cycles. The logic does not query the minimum ID, so it wastes time on all ID ranges before the first actual user.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Query both `SELECT MIN(id), MAX(id)` from the users table and use the actual bounds as range endpoints. Alternatively, switch to cursor-based pagination with `WHERE id > ? ORDER BY id LIMIT ?` to handle sparse or non-zero-based IDs efficiently.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: No exception handling for database operations
DESCRIPTION: The code does not catch or handle `sqlite3.OperationalError`, `sqlite3.IntegrityError`, or other database exceptions. A constraint violation, schema mismatch, database lock, or disk full error will crash the script abruptly without cleanup, meaningful error messages, or the ability to retry/resume. The caller has no visibility into which batch was being processed when the error occurred.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Wrap database operations in explicit exception handlers for `sqlite3.Error` types. Log the error with context (batch number, current IDs), ensure `conn.rollback()` is called, and allow graceful failure/resumption.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: data
TITLE: Hardcoded tier value 'free' has no configurability or validation
DESCRIPTION: Every unbackfilled user is set to `'free'` regardless of business logic. If some users should receive a different tier based on payment history, creation date, or other flags, this migration silently overwrites those values. Additionally, there is no validation that `'free'` is a valid enum value if the schema enforces enumerated tiers.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Document the assumption explicitly in a comment or configuration. Consider deriving the tier value from existing user data. If the schema enforces enumerated tiers, add a CHECK constraint or validation before the update.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Negative max_id causes silent skip of all rows
DESCRIPTION: If the `users` table contains only negative IDs (e.g., legacy or test data), `max_id` will be negative. `range(0, max_id, BATCH_SIZE)` with a negative upper bound produces an empty sequence, causing the migration to silently skip all rows without any warning.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Validate that `max_id > 0` and raise an informative error if not. Alternatively, switch pagination to `SELECT id FROM users WHERE tier IS NULL` to handle negative IDs correctly.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: No logging of migration progress or completion
DESCRIPTION: The function returns a count but produces no log output. For a migration processing thousands or millions of rows, the operator has no visibility into progress, estimated time remaining, or which batch is being processed. If the process is killed, there is no record of what was completed.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add `logging` calls at the start of migration, after each batch completion, and at the end, including batch number, cumulative row count, and timestamps.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Connection creation has no error handling
DESCRIPTION: `sqlite3.connect(db_path)` can raise `sqlite3.OperationalError` if the path is invalid or permissions are insufficient. Additionally, no `journal_mode`, `timeout`, or `busy_handler` is configured, which can cause `database is locked` errors if another process accesses the file concurrently.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Wrap `sqlite3.connect()` in a try/except block with a descriptive error message. Consider setting `timeout` to allow waiting for locked databases, and optionally set `journal_mode='WAL'` for concurrent access scenarios.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Affected row counts are ignored
DESCRIPTION: `conn.execute()` returns a cursor with a `rowcount` attribute, but the code discards it without checking. If a user ID is deleted between SELECT and UPDATE, or if the table schema changes, the update silently fails with `rowcount == 0`, and the code proceeds without detecting the discrepancy.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check `cursor.rowcount` after each `UPDATE` and log a warning if the count is unexpectedly low or zero.

---END---

SEVERITY: critical
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Niezatwierdzone transakcje powodują utratę danych
DESCRIPTION: Połączenia SQLite domyślnie działają w trybie transakcyjnym. Kod aktualizuje wiersze, ale nigdy nie wywołuje `conn.commit()`. CATEGORY: logic

CATEGORY: logic

SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: concurrency

SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: max_id + 1 nigdy nie jest włączony — błąd off-by-one na górnej granicy

SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: Brak logowania postępu lub wskazania statusu migracji
DESCRIPTION: Dla backfill mogącego dotknąć miliony wierszy, brak logowania postępu, szacunkowego czasu zakończenia czy błędów. Operator uruchamiający migrację nie ma widoczności czy działa, jest zawieszony czy prawie gotowy. Niejawne migracje trudno audytować post-hoc.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Dodaj okresowe logowanie (np. co N partii) raportujące całkowitą ilość przetworzonych wierszy i czas upłynięty. Używaj modułu `logging` a nie `print`, i uwzględnij czas startu i przetworzoną prędkość.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: concurrency
TITLE: Niejawne zachowanie transakcji zależy od wersji Python sqlite3
DESCRIPTION: Moduł sqlite3 Pythona zmienił domyślne zachowanie izolacji w wersji 3.12. Poleganie na niejawnym zarządzaniu transakcjami sprawia, że kod jest zależny od wersji i potencjalnie niebezpieczny dla dostępu konkurencyjnego.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Jawnie ustaw `isolation_level=None` lub `isolation_level='DEFERRED'` przy tworzeniu połączenia i zarządzaj transakcjami ręcznie za pomocą jawnych `commit()` i `rollback()`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: range() pomija ID poniżej 0 — obsługa ujemnych ID
DESCRIPTION: Jeśli jakikolwiek użytkownik ma ujemny `id` (możliwy z pewnymi konfiguracjami ORM lub wstawieniami ręcznymi), range zaczyna od 0 i te wiersze nigdy nie są odwiedzane. Anchor `MAX(id)` nie ma wpływu na ujemne ID, więc są trwale wykluczane.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Zamień strategię opartą na range na podejście cursor-based, które nie zakłada nieujemnych i sekwencyjnych ID. Użyj `SELECT id FROM users WHERE tier IS NULL ORDER BY id` aby obsługać wszystkie wartości ID.

raw:
Poniżej znajduje się zdeduplicowana lista wyników z trzema niezależnymi recenzjami. Scalono duplikaty (to samo usterka, inne sformułowanie), zachowując wszystkie unikalne wyniki.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Numeric type coercion is broken for various formats
DESCRIPTION: Multiple issues prevent correct numeric type detection:
1. `str.isdigit()` returns `False` for negative integers like `"-1"` or `"-42"` because the hyphen is not a digit, causing them to be stored as strings.
2. `str.isdigit()` returns `True` for Unicode superscript digits (e.g., `²`, `³`) and other non-ASCII digit characters, which may cause unexpected coercion or errors.
3. The float regex `^-?\d+\.\d+$` requires a decimal point and digits on both sides, so it rejects valid formats like `-5`, `+3.5`, `.5`, and `5.`, all falling back to strings.
Combined, these issues cause silent type mismatches where numeric values are stored as strings instead of being properly coerced to `int` or `float`.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace regex-based type detection with try/except blocks: `try: int(value) ... try: float(value)` for robust numeric coercion.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: Broad exception catching hides errors and masks failures
DESCRIPTION: Both the file-read `except Exception` and per-line `except Exception: pass` catch every possible error (including `MemoryError`, `UnicodeDecodeError`, filesystem errors, syntax errors, etc.) and silently discard them. File read failures, permissions errors, and syntax errors all produce an empty or partial dict with no indication that anything went wrong. This makes debugging extremely difficult.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Catch specific exceptions (`FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError`, `ValueError`, `UnicodeDecodeError`). Log or re-raise unexpected errors. Do not silently catch broad `Exception` on the file-read path.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: No file encoding specified; platform-dependent behavior
DESCRIPTION: `Path.read_text()` without an explicit `encoding` argument uses the platform default encoding (e.g., `cp1252` on Windows, `utf-8` on Linux). The same config file can parse differently or raise `UnicodeDecodeError` depending on the OS. Combined with broad exception catching, these errors are silently swallowed.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Pass `encoding="utf-8"` explicitly to `Path.read_text()` to ensure consistent cross-platform behavior.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Lines without colons are not validated, creating malformed entries
DESCRIPTION: `str.partition(":")` on a line with no colon returns `(line, "", "")`. The parser stores this as a key-value pair with the entire line as the key and an empty string as the value, silently inserting garbage entries into the config dict instead of treating malformed lines as errors.
SUGGESTED_FIX: After `partition`, check that the separator is not empty; if empty, skip the line with a warning or raise an error.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Path traversal vulnerability — no validation on input paths
DESCRIPTION: Both `parse_config` and `merge_configs` accept arbitrary string paths without validation. A caller supplying user-controlled input could read arbitrary files on the filesystem (e.g., `../../etc/shadow`). If ever exposed to untrusted input, this becomes a file-read vulnerability.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Validate that the resolved path is within an expected directory using `Path.resolve()` and checking it starts with an allowed base path.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: merge_configs doesn't properly signal file errors to caller
DESCRIPTION: If `override_path` fails to read (permissions, missing file, corrupt data), `parse_config` silently returns `{}` and the merged result is just the base config with no indication that the override was not applied. The caller believes the merge succeeded when it actually failed.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Have `parse_config` raise an exception or return a sentinel value on file-read errors so the caller can distinguish "empty config" from "failed to read".

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Duplicate keys silently overwritten without warning
DESCRIPTION: If the same key appears multiple times in a single config file, later occurrences silently overwrite earlier ones with no warning or error. This can mask configuration errors where a user accidentally duplicates a key with a different value, leading to hard-to-debug behavior.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Track seen keys and either raise an error or emit a warning when a duplicate is detected.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Keys containing colons are mis-parsed in YAML-like nested syntax
DESCRIPTION: The parser splits on the first colon only using `partition(":")`. Keys with colons (e.g., YAML nested syntax `parent:child: value`) are mis-parsed with only the part before the first colon used as the key (e.g., key becomes `parent` instead of `parent:child`).
SUGGESTED_FIX: Document this limitation clearly, or implement proper hierarchical key-value parsing to support nested structures.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Empty key after stripping is accepted
DESCRIPTION: A line like `: some_value` produces an empty-string key `""` in the resulting dict. This is almost certainly unintentional and could cause subtle downstream bugs when code looks up config values.
SUGGESTED_FIX: After stripping the key, check `if not key: continue` to skip entries with blank keys.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: data
TITLE: String "none"/"null" not coerced to None
DESCRIPTION: YAML-like configs commonly use `none`, `null`, or `~` to represent null values. This parser stores them as literal strings, which may surprise callers who expect Python `None`.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Add a check for `value.lower() in ("none", "null", "~")` and map to `None`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: In-place mutation of base config in merge_configs
DESCRIPTION: `base.update(override)` mutates the `base` dictionary in place. Callers expecting a new merged dict will inadvertently modify the original object, causing unexpected side effects and hidden state changes.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Return `base.copy()` or `{**base, **override}` to avoid mutating the input dictionary.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Inline comments treated as part of values
DESCRIPTION: Lines like `key: value # comment` are parsed as `key` with value `value # comment` because the parser only strips leading/trailing whitespace, not inline comments. Inline comments corrupt the value data.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Strip inline comments by finding the first `#` character, or document that inline comments are unsupported.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: UTF-8 BOM corrupts first configuration key
DESCRIPTION: Files starting with a UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (`\ufeff`) cause the first key to retain the invisible BOM character, leading to mismatched keys during lookups. For example, `key: value` with BOM becomes `\ufeffkey: value`.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Strip the BOM using `text.lstrip('\ufeff')` after reading the file.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Misleading "YAML-like" claim with flat-only parsing
DESCRIPTION: The docstring claims YAML-like support, but the parser only handles flat key-value pairs. It lacks indentation handling, nested structures, lists, and multi-line strings.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Update the docstring to accurately describe the parser's capabilities or use a proper YAML library like `PyYAML`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: performance
TITLE: Unused line number enumeration wastes computation
DESCRIPTION: `enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1)` calculates line numbers that are never used in the loop body, wasting CPU cycles on every line processed.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Remove the line number enumeration or use `text.splitlines()` without `enumerate`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Quoted strings retain surrounding quotes in parsed values
DESCRIPTION: Values wrapped in quotes (e.g., `key: "value"`) are stored with the quotes intact, requiring downstream code to manually strip them. This is likely unintended and complicates value handling.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Implement quote stripping logic to remove surrounding quotes and handle escaped characters.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Boolean coercion misses common YAML true/false variants
DESCRIPTION: The parser only recognizes `true` and `false`, ignoring standard YAML boolean aliases like `yes`, `no`, `on`, and `off`.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Expand the boolean check to include `("yes", "no", "on", "off")` alongside `true` and `false`.

---END---

I notice the **Reviewer qwen report** section is empty—no findings provided there.

Since there's only one reviewer's report, I'll deduplicate within it (removing the finding that the sonnet reviewer themselves marked as non-bug) and output all remaining findings:

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Empty key accepted when line starts with colon
DESCRIPTION: When `line.partition(":")` is called on a line like `:value`, the key becomes an empty string `""` after stripping. This silently inserts `{"": value}` into the config dict, which is almost certainly unintended and can mask malformed input.
SUGGESTED_FIX: After computing `key`, add `if not key: continue` (or raise/log) before inserting into `config`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Negative integers not coerced to int
DESCRIPTION: `value.isdigit()` returns `False` for negative numbers like `"-42"` because `-` is not a digit. These values fall through to the `else` branch and are stored as strings, silently breaking any caller that expects an integer.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace `value.isdigit()` with a try/except around `int(value)`, or use `re.match(r'^-?\d+$', value)` before calling `int()`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Float regex rejects negative floats and scientific notation
DESCRIPTION: The pattern `r"^-?\d+\.\d+$"` handles negative floats (the `-?` is present) but rejects scientific notation like `1e10`, `1.5e-3`, and values without a fractional part like `1.` or `.5`. Such values are silently stored as strings instead of floats.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `try: config[key] = float(value)` with a fallback rather than a regex, or extend the pattern to cover scientific notation: `r'^-?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][+-]?\d+)?$'`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: Silent exception swallowing hides parse errors
DESCRIPTION: Both the outer `except Exception: return config` and the inner `except Exception: pass` discard all error information. A corrupt file, a permissions error, a UnicodeDecodeError, or a logic bug in the parser all produce the same result: a silently incomplete config. Callers have no way to distinguish a missing file from a valid empty config.
SUGGESTED_FIX: At minimum log the error (`logging.warning(...)`) and re-raise or return a sentinel. For file-open errors, let `OSError`/`FileNotFoundError` propagate so callers can handle them explicitly.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Line with no colon stores entire line as key with empty value
DESCRIPTION: If a config line contains no `:`, `partition(":")` returns `(line, "", "")`, so `key = line` and `value = ""`. The empty string hits the `else` branch and is stored as `config[line] = ""`. This silently treats a bare word (or a malformed line) as a valid key mapped to an empty string.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check whether `partition` found a separator: `key, sep, value = line.partition(":"); if not sep: continue`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: No file size limit allows memory exhaustion
DESCRIPTION: `Path(path).read_text()` reads the entire file into memory before parsing. A caller passing an untrusted path (e.g., `/dev/zero`, a multi-GB log file, or a symlink to a large file) will exhaust process memory with no upper bound enforced.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check `Path(path).stat().st_size` before reading and reject files above a reasonable threshold (e.g., 1 MB for a config file).

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: No encoding specified; behavior is platform-dependent
DESCRIPTION: `Path.read_text()` without an `encoding` argument uses the platform default (`locale.getpreferredencoding()`), which varies between Windows and Linux. A config file saved as UTF-8 on Linux may raise `UnicodeDecodeError` on Windows (or vice versa), and that error is silently swallowed, returning an empty dict.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Always pass `encoding="utf-8"` (or `"utf-8-sig"` to strip BOM): `Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Duplicate keys silently overwritten; last value wins
DESCRIPTION: If the same key appears multiple times in the file, each occurrence overwrites the previous one without any warning. Depending on intended semantics (e.g., lists, errors), this may silently lose data.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Either warn when a duplicate key is detected or document that last-value-wins is intentional.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: `line_num` variable is computed but never used
DESCRIPTION: `enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1)` binds `line_num`, but it is never referenced in the loop body or in error messages. This is dead code and a missed opportunity for diagnostics.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Either use `line_num` in error/warning messages when skipping malformed lines, or replace `enumerate(...)` with a plain `for raw in text.splitlines():`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: `merge_configs` returns empty dict silently if both files missing
DESCRIPTION: If both paths are missing or unreadable, `parse_config` returns `{}` for each, and `merge_configs` returns `{}` with no indication that anything went wrong. Callers cannot distinguish a successful merge of two empty configs from a total read failure.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Propagate exceptions from `parse_config`, or have `merge_configs` validate that at least one file was readable.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Keys with only whitespace stored after stripping
DESCRIPTION: A line like `   : value` has `key = ""` after stripping, which the empty-key check (once added) would catch. But a line like `  \t  : value` also strips to `""`. Without the guard these produce `{"": value}`. This is covered by the empty-key finding but worth noting that tab-only keys follow the same path.
SUGGESTED_FIX: The same `if not key: continue` guard from the empty-key finding covers this case.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: data
TITLE: Boolean check is case-insensitive but float/int checks are not
DESCRIPTION: `value.lower() in ("true", "false")` handles `True`, `TRUE`, `tRuE`, etc. But there is no equivalent flexibility for integers or floats. This inconsistency may surprise users who expect uniform case handling.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Document the case sensitivity rules, or apply consistent normalization across all type checks.
